correctness.rationale: For \(\alpha+\beta=2\), the matrix identity \(A+A^{\mathsf T}=2J\) implies exactly logistic total biomass \(\dot S=S(1-S)\). The normalized dynamics are a skew-symmetric zero-sum three-species replicator scaled by \(S\) plus symmetric mutation \(\mu(1-3p_i)\). The exact KL identity \(\dot H=-\mu D\) and compact KL sublevels give \(3H\le D\le C(H_0)H\). Infinite cumulative exposure forces \(H\to0\); quadratic expansions \(H\sim(3/2)\|\delta\|^2\) and \(D\sim9\|\delta\|^2\) yield the sharp logarithmic rate \(-6\). Finite exposure yields \(h_\infty>0\); each positive entropy level is a simple closed nonstationary orbit of the unmutated vector field, and integrable tail perturbations with \(S(t)\to1\) imply every forward shift of any omega-limit point belongs to that limit, proving the entire curve. All boundary cases and hypotheses are in RESULT.md. The verification program checks exact identities using rational arithmetic and numerical finite examples, not the infinite-time theorem.

originality.rationale: A statement-level comparison with the full original 2022 May–Leonard constant-mutator paper, 2015 rock-paper-scissors mutator analysis, and 2019 zero-sum cycle theorem, plus semantically retrieved related mathematical claims, found no covering arbitrary-measurable-schedule cumulative-budget dichotomy or universal sharp per-budget exponent. The unmutated cycles and constant-rate stable equilibrium are explicitly known components; only their nonautonomous coupling and exact threshold are attributed to the present contribution. Priority risk for a general nonautonomous replicator perturbation theorem remains.
residual_risks: Broad general nonautonomous replicator–mutator convergence theorems might imply the result by specialization despite the lack of an identical indexed statement.
Search and available published summaries cannot certify global publication priority or uniqueness.
The mutation-free periodicity and constant-mutation stabilization themselves are not novel.

The 2018 two-patch time-varying migration article was abstract-inspected only; although its varying diffusion and one-way mutation differ from the present symmetric mutation budget, full-text content was unavailable.

value.rationale: The all-schedule sharp dichotomy answers whether a time-vanishing mutation intervention truly destroys or merely changes the amplitude of neutral biodiversity oscillations. It separates finite total transition exposure from sustained cumulative exposure without assuming decay monotonicity or regularity, identifies the whole omega-limit set rather than merely nonconvergence, and gives a universal quantitative rate and exact power-law boundary. These are direct motivated ecological questions at the model’s critical competition line, not ad hoc numerical constants.
